2.1.evidence: A person who contravenes an order issued under this Act shall be Offence and guilty of an offence and is liable to a fine not exceeding P5 000 or to penalty imprisonment for a term not exceeding 2 years or to both.
2.1.rationale: The framework creates a criminal offence for contravening an order issued under the Act and specifies criminal sanctions (fine and/or imprisonment). This establishes criminal penalties connected to domestic-violence-related protective orders.
2.1.evidence_original: A person who contravenes an order issued under this Act shall be Offence and guilty of an offence and is liable to a fine not exceeding P5 000 or to penalty imprisonment for a term not exceeding 2 years or to both.

2.2.evidence:
In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires - "applicant" means any person who alleges to have been subjected to an act of domestic violence; "child" includes biological, adopted, step or any child in the care or custody of the applicant or respondent; "court" means a magistrate's court of any rank, and includes a customary court which has been authorised, by Statutory Instrument, to hear a matter under this Act; "domestic relationship" means a relationship between an applicant and the respondent in any of the followirig ways -
An occupation order shall grant the applicant or child the exclusive order or non exclusive right to live in the residence occupied or belonging to the applicant, the respondent or to the applicant and the respondent, for a specified or indefinite period.
An order issued under this Act shall remain in force unless it order expires or is revoked under section 13.
A person who contravenes an order issued under this Act shall be Offence and guilty of an offence and is liable to a fine not exceeding P5 000 or to penalty imprisonment for a term not exceeding 2 years or to both.
2.2.rationale: The text defines who may apply (an "applicant" alleging domestic violence), identifies the issuing authority (a "court"), provides for order duration (specified/indefinite period and continuing force unless expired/revoked), and sets a criminal consequence for breach (offence with fine/imprisonment).
2.2.evidence_original:
In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires - "applicant" means any person who alleges to have been subjected to an act of domestic violence; "child" includes biological, adopted, step or any child in the care or custody of the applicant or respondent; "court" means a magistrate's court of any rank, and includes a customary court which has been authorised, by Statutory Instrument, to hear a matter under this Act; "domestic relationship" means a relationship between an applicant and the respondent in any of the followirig ways -

An occupation order shall grant the applicant or child the exclusive order or non exclusive right to live in the residence occupied or belonging to the applicant, the respondent or to the applicant and the respondent, for a specified or indefinite period.

An order issued under this Act shall remain in force unless it order expires or is revoked under section 13.

A person who contravenes an order issued under this Act shall be Offence and guilty of an offence and is liable to a fine not exceeding P5 000 or to penalty imprisonment for a term not exceeding 2 years or to both.
